What Problem Does NeuroLoop Solve? (In Plain English)
In spinal cord and dorsal-horn neuromodulation, patients fall into different hidden biological types (Phenotypes): some get lasting pain relief (Responders), some get zero benefit (Nonresponders), and some develop Delayed Worsening (Hyperalgesia) where continued stimulation causes intracellular chloride (Cl⁻) accumulation and increases pain over time. Standard open-loop or fixed-calibration controllers keep stimulating blindly. C5_SequentialBayesian tracks the physical dose actually delivered to the tissue, asks sparse high-value pain questions only when uncertain, updates a 3-hypothesis probability belief, and automatically shuts off stimulation when it detects non-response or delayed worsening.

How to Read the 5 Virtual Patient Phenotypes

1. Responder (responder)

Benefits from moderate burst or conventional tonic stimulation. Goal: maintain analgesic relief while minimizing patient query fatigue and managing habituation.

2. Nonresponder (nonresponder)

Has near-zero analgesic sensitivity. Stimulating only wastes electrical energy and incurs effort penalties. Goal: detect lack of benefit early and abstain (turn OFF).

3. Delayed Worsening (delayed_worsening)

The hardest clinical trap: stimulation builds up delayed sensitization (or collapses KCC2 chloride extrusion in Engine A), causing pain to spike. Goal: detect rising pain under active exposure and immediately shut OFF.

4. Null Effect (null_effect)

Analytic zero-gain control fixture: stimulation has literally zero biological effect on analgesia, habituation, or sensitization. Goal: verify the controller does not hallucinate benefit.

5. Random Fault Window (random_fault_window)

A responder who experiences an unpredictable multi-step electrode impedance spike (lead migration / lift-off). Goal: latch stimulation OFF during the fault and safely resume after 2 clean steps.

How Do We Know the Bayesian Controller Isn't Just Lucky? (The 3 Causal Ablations)

Every benchmark run tests C5_SequentialBayesian alongside three surgically crippled versions of itself on the exact same patients:

Ablation 1: Frozen Beliefs (C5_Ablation_FrozenBeliefs)

Locks the probability belief at the initial prior [50% Resp, 30% Nonresp, 20% Worsening]. Result: Delayed-worsening loss explodes from 372.59 → 503.67 because it never learns the patient is worsening.

Ablation 2: Shuffled Reports (C5_Ablation_ShuffledReports)

Updates beliefs, but scrambles the patient pain numbers. Result: Responder loss degrades from 263.01 → 321.68 and Worsening degrades to 436.52, proving the controller relies on the true causal link between delivered dose and pain report.

Ablation 3: Matched Query Schedule (C5_Ablation_MatchedSchedule)

Asks questions on the exact same schedule and computes the posterior, but ignores the posterior when picking actions. Result: Worsening loss jumps to 481.41, proving that acting on the posterior belief is what saves the patient.

What is Counterfactual Twin Branching?
In real life, you can never know what would have happened if you had turned the stimulator OFF or switched programs 4 minutes ago. In NeuroLoop, at steps k = 8, 16, 24, 32, the simulator clones the exact patient state and random noise streams into parallel Counterfactual Twins and tests four alternative policies (u_OFF, u_HOLD, u_CAL_BEST, u_LOW_DUTY) over future horizons H = 4, 8, 16 steps. Excess Regret (R̂_H) measures how much worse the controller did than the best hindsight comparator (0.00 means optimal!).
